audit.reasoning: The record excludes Yele from fixed-stress sets, against StressTyp2's initial+alternating coding. I verified the basis in two held primary sources: Henderson 1995:5 (3-syllable words are stressed on syllable 1 unless V2 is more open than V1 or the word is vowel-initial, then syllable 2; 4-syllable words 1st+3rd; 5-syllable words do not occur) and Levinson 2022 sec. 3.4 pp.66-67, the current 587-pp reference grammar, which quotes Henderson, calls the rules essentially correct, adds further vowel-quality and lexical conditioning and clitic-induced pre-clitic stress, and says more research is needed. Placement therefore depends on vowel quality/onset, not a fixed count from an edge, so the exclusion is sound and no better source exists (Levinson 2022 cites no stress study; fetched sources Henderson 1975:819 is a superseded tentative 'initial stress' note that explains the database coding). sources.quote: 'Word stress appears to be predictable, and consists of loudness and slight rise in pitch on the stressed syllable. It falls on the first syllable of the unaffixed phonological word ... The stress pattern of reduplicated words is the same as for two phonological words, but with a heavier stress on the first part. ... Stress patterns in longer words have not been studied fully, but no contrastive stress patterns have been observed.'
